fields.label: Name
fields.description: A human-readable name, e.g. MR.ERP DMS

fields.label: Adapter
fields.description: Which system is on the other side. Values follow the legacy product (webhook | xero | flowaccount | mrerp | mrerp_dms | express); the new platform only implements mrerp_dms for now — the rest are listed so the contract does not change silently.

fields.label: Owner Account
fields.description: Whose connection this is. **Empty = a site-wide shared connection** (configured by the owner, using an account that has the rights); filled = one operator's own connection. In the legacy product every operator had their own DMS connection, with the owner's acting as the template.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Once disabled it takes no part in pushes (in the legacy product, disabling was the gate that kept a batch from going to the wrong place).

fields.label: Default Connection
fields.description: Only one default per account + adapter (the legacy product's unique index).

fields.label: System URL
fields.description: The sign-in URL, e.g. for MR.ERP DMS. The legacy product hard-coded and hid this for DMS (there was only one instance); we keep it editable so switching instances later needs no code change.

fields.label: Password
fields.description: A native Frappe Password field, encrypted at rest (equivalent to the legacy encrypt_str + KMS); the API never echoes it back.

fields.label: Account With Write Access
fields.description: The legacy product's own words: this set of credentials is used to connect, look up, create and rewrite; sales people still use their own account to match the commission owner, and the server falls back to the owner's credentials when a customer record has to be rewritten. So business writes go through this set, not the operator's own credentials.

fields.label: Auto Push
fields.description: The legacy product keeps this off for this connection (the whole path is manual: wizard plus a confirmation dialog).

DMS booking defaults (JSON): model/colour/branch/team/delivery days, plus the **pinned advisor**.

The advisor field is the sales-commission owner: if the account matches a name in the DMS advisor roster it is assigned automatically; only when it does not match (the owner's shared account, a data-entry clerk) does the advisor_id here pin it. Pinning wins over every match.
